name: RI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Gabe Amo runs in a D+12 district
Huge money gap: $1.85M cash on hand vs about $2,300 for Keenan
Markets price a Democratic hold near 96%; no competitive polling exists
No outside spending active on either side
model.rationale: Amo's incumbency in a D+12 seat plus a cash advantage of roughly 800-to-1 over an essentially unfunded Republican challenger leaves no plausible upset path; fundamentals and prediction markets both point to a safe Democratic hold.
model.watch: A late scandal or a surprise wave of outside spending against Amo could narrow the margin, though the district's lean makes the outcome very unlikely to change.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rhode Island's first district leans heavily Democratic, and incumbent Gabe Amo is seeking re-election with the advantages that status brings. He has raised about $1.7 million and holds $1.85 million on hand, while Republican nominee Kellie Keenan has raised roughly $13,000 and reports about $2,300 in cash. No outside groups are active on either side, and no public polls have surveyed the general election. An independent candidate, Pedro DeSouza, is also on the ballot.

Prediction markets give the Democratic side roughly a 96 percent chance of holding the seat. With the incumbent well funded, the challenger essentially unfunded, and a partisan lean of about twelve points Democratic, the race sits firmly in the safe Democratic category. The realistic question is the size of the winning margin, not which party controls the seat.
